answer_md:
🐾 Here’s the story behind Matt’s **Norfolk Southern** work.

From **November 2019** to **September 2023**, Matt led Revenue and Shipment Planning modernization as a Director at **Accenture**. It was the Cloud Innovation Center’s first engagement. The railroad’s mainframe dated to the **1970s**: orders could fall out unnoticed until customers called, business rules lived in COBOL and assembly, and clerks manually handled waybill and rating fallout through green-screen consoles. Wholesale replacement was too risky for systems carrying live rail operations. Meanwhile, the client organization was accustomed to mainframe thinking, account leadership to waterfall, and Matt’s team was learning a new working model during COVID.

Matt started with domain-driven design and event storming to map business functions and dependencies. He used the Boris Exercise to map APIs and data flows, and SNAP-E documentation to capture dependencies and risks. Rather than a big-bang cutover, he kept the mainframe as the system of record while APIs, microservices, and CockroachDB rose beside it. Change data capture synchronized the platforms; reconciliation reports checked that no functionality or data was lost. API gateways and anti-corruption layers supported incremental replacement, with Docker, Kubernetes, TDD, and automated CI/CD supporting delivery.

When the client grew restless for tangible progress, Matt brought its revenue management team into the innovation hub to co-create the Shipper Revenue System UI. They worked from personas through high-fidelity prototypes in weekly build-measure-learn iterations. He also led a **2-day** CIC Academy course, delivered twice monthly over **6 months**. Pair programming faced explicit resistance; Matt let participants experience it firsthand, then used “I do, we do, you do” to spread scarce domain knowledge.

The UI MVP launched covering **95%** of its targeted use cases, capturing real orders with clean data feeding the mainframe. EDI validation caught fallout proactively and notified trading partners. Client contributors learned to own their backlog and gained Angular, Node, Spring Boot, and cloud-native skills to support the application after **Accenture** rolled off.

answer_md:
🐾 Here’s what Matt worked on at **RBC**.

From June **2012** to June **2013**, Matt served as a Senior Technology Architecture Manager at **Accenture** on **RBC’s** Day**2Day** Corporate Banking modernization. The bank was evaluating Bottomline WebSeries as its payment hub engine while planning to replace **RBC Express**. Existing systems had performance and scalability limitations, lacked mobile cheque deposit, offered limited cross-device access, and had no API integration with external financial applications. Leadership needed to know whether the proposed platform could meet business requirements before committing further investment.

Matt conducted an architecture assessment and gap/fit analysis using code reviews, stakeholder interviews, documentation analysis, and architectural heat maps. He assessed Data, Application, Technology, and Business Architecture, then worked with the bank’s enterprise architecture team on target-system models and a cost-to-fix versus benefit comparison. The assessment found that WebSeries lacked the modularity required for **RBC’s** long-term digital operating model. That finding prevented further investment in a platform path that could not deliver and enabled the bank to redirect technical resources toward higher-priority initiatives.

Alongside that assessment, Matt established the PMO. He created the project management plan, program reporting, risk and dependency management, and centralized communications across **RBC**, **Accenture**, and Bottomline Technologies. Designated team contacts, real-time updates, daily summaries, and a task-tracking matrix eliminated missed program updates, reduced redundant effort, and clarified resource assignments.

When the previous data conversion lead left early in the initiative, Matt took over the workstream from scratch. He analyzed legacy payment records, documented source-to-target transformation rules, planned mock conversion cycles, and established reconciliation checks for payment amounts and beneficiary details. He managed onshore and offshore teams performing data scrubbing and validation.

He also delivered a mobile modernization blueprint covering API integration, cheque deposit requirements, and cross-browser and cross-device scalability. The deliverables included the architecture assessment, PMO framework, end-to-end conversion plan, and mobile implementation roadmap.
